questions.stem: Consider this: A landowner drafting a will creates a life estate. The condition is morally objectionable. Which statement best states the governing legal rule on these facts?

options.text: A life tenant may sell the property in fee simple whenever they wish on these facts.
options.misconception: assumes the life tenant owns forever

options.text: A remainder holder is entitled to possession during the life tenant's lifetime on these facts.
options.misconception: treats the remainder as a present right

options.text: A remainder returns to the grantor while a reversion goes to a third party on these facts.
options.misconception: confuses a remainder with a reversion

options.text: A life estate gives the holder possession for the duration of a life, with a remainder to another who takes possession when that life ends on these facts.

questions.explanation: Estates divide time. The life tenant has the present right of possession, and the remainderman has a future interest that becomes possessory when the measuring life ends, while any residue left in the grantor is a reversion. Here the decisive point is the life estate and remainder, so the result follows from that doctrine rather than from the surface appeal of a competing statement. Each distractor rests on a different mistake about how the doctrine operates.
questions.hint: Ask who possesses now and who possesses later. Keep the inquiry on the life estate and remainder.
